verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents headless operation directly. The docs say that in CI and other headless environments you authenticate with a personal API key instead of the browser flow. jitsu-cli "does everything the UI does" and accepts `-h`/`-k` credential flags, alongside a programmatic Management API and a repo-based `jitsu-cli deploy` workflow for Functions. Missing for 10: a documented end-to-end CI pipeline recipe (e.g., GitHub Actions example) for the CLI, and independent or hands-on corroboration of CI usage; the OpenAPI spec probe also returned 404 at standard paths.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: In CI and other headless environments the browser flow can't run. There you authenticate with a personal API key instead
**`jitsu-cli`** — a real command-line interface that does everything the UI does.
Saves credentials so subsequent commands don't need `-h` / `-k`.
build and deploy them from your own repo with the Jitsu CLI — `jitsu-cli init` scaffolds a TypeScript project with tests, and `jitsu-cli deploy` ships it to your workspace.
Jitsu exposes an HTTP API for managing workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions.
